#9784. Your Vercel AI SDK agent already knows the answer. Stop making it re-derive it.

Your Vercel AI SDK agent just spent 3.9 seconds and a full tool loop answering a goal it answered yesterday. Different user, slightly different wording, same intent — and the agent re-derived the whole plan from scratch: same tool choices, same order, same result. The model call isn't the expensive part. The re-derivation is.

This is the loop tax, and it hits every framework the same way. Vercel AI SDK's generateText with tools, Mastra's agent runs, a hand-rolled loop — they all re-run the same goals all day, because nothing in the stack notices that the trajectory repeated. Prompt caching at the model layer saves you per-call. It doesn't notice that the plan repeated.

Pomerene is a deterministic trajectory cache for agentic workflows, and the integration model is deliberately boring: it wraps your agent function, not your model client. Your prompts are never touched, rewritten, or intercepted. That matters for Vercel AI SDK and Mastra, because the cache doesn't need to know anything about your framework's internals — only that it can record a run and replay the recorded steps when a matching goal arrives.

There are two integration shapes, and both are framework-proof — the same code works whether your agent runs on Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, LangGraph, or a hand-rolled loop, because the unit being cached is the trajectory, not the framework object.

L1 returns the cached outcome. L2 resumes your agent mid-trajectory. A miss runs live and gets stored. That's the whole integration — and it works the same way in a Vercel AI SDK tool loop as in a Mastra agent, because in both cases the agent is a function: goal in, result out, plus a recorded trajectory in between.

Three outcomes, all deterministic — hashing plus vector geometry computed in TypeScript, no LLM call in the match decision, so the same input makes the same cache decision every time:

On τ-bench — the airline customer-service benchmark, dense with the rephrased-same-goal traffic that support agents actually see — the engine served 86% of paraphrased requests from cache, with 78% of those judged correct. Read both numbers honestly: 86% is why repetitive agent workloads are worth caching, and 78% is why the write-safety rules below are the product, not a footnote.

A Vercel AI SDK agent with tools can charge a card, send a message, mutate a database. A Mastra agent the same. So the write rule is the whole product: steps that write are never fuzzy-matched against a new request. A cached write step replays only on an exact goal-plus-context repeat; anything ambiguous becomes a miss or an L2 handoff. Partial drift produces a handoff to your agent, never a subtly wrong execution. On an adversarial eval of polarity-flipped pairs (requests that are semantically close but must not be confused, like activate vs. deactivate at 0.853 cosine similarity), the gated engine produced 0 false positives across 18 pairs.

One honest note, because the gate's story changed after the first post about it: the write-safety gate as originally published had three holes, found via outside critique and fixed in core — merged, shipping in the next core release. An abstract-goal match is no longer treated as an exact repeat (write trajectories are refused there, and context is diffed); a trajectory with no taint records plus a context change is now a miss; and a hit never serves past a declared external_write — control hands back to the agent at that step. Still open, not shipped: entity agreement on read matches. The numbers above describe the gate as designed; the fixes are what keep the design honest, and the open item is the next gate to build.

If your agent's traffic is mostly unique, one-off tasks, this buys you less — and the kit will tell you that before you commit. The built-in diagnostics (/v1/diagnostics) show hit rates, the L1/L2/miss breakdown, latency percentiles, and dollars and tokens saved for your real traffic. If your traces show the same goals arriving in different wording, you're paying the model to rediscover plans it already derived. A wrapper turns that rediscovery into a replay — in your Vercel AI SDK loop, your Mastra agent, or wherever the agent lives.

Pomerene ships as a self-hosted Starter Kit — Indie $99 / Pro $249, one-time, source included — so the cache runs in your infrastructure, next to your agents. Quickstart is about 5 minutes (Node 20+, Docker or Postgres 15+). Docs and details at pomerene.io/starter-kit.

You can upload your own photos from your computer or from Google Drive, and add them to Canva's templates using a simple drag-and-drop interface. Canva is a great tool for small business owners, online entrepreneurs, and marketers who don’t have the time and want to edit quickly.

To create sophisticated graphics, a tool such as Photoshop can is ideal. To use it, you’ll need to learn its hundreds of features, get familiar with the software, and it’s best to have a good background in design, too.

So here  Canva takes place, with Canva you can do all that with drag-and-drop feature. It’s also easier to use and free. Also an even-more-affordable paid version is available for $12.95 per month.

The product is available in three plans: Free, Pro ($12.99/month per user or  $119.99/year for up to 5 people), and Enterprise ($30 per user per month, minimum 25 people).

To get started on Canva, you will need to create an account by providing your email address, Google, Facebook or Apple credentials. You will then choose your account type between student, teacher, small business, large company, non-profit, or personal. Based on your choice of account type, templates will be recommended to you.

You can sign up for a free trial of Canva Pro, or you can start with the free version to get a sense of whether it’s the right graphic design tool for your needs.

When you sign up for an account, Canva will suggest different post types to choose from. Based on the type of account you set up  you'll be able to see templates categorized by the following categories: social media posts, documents, presentations, marketing, events, ads, launch your business, build your online brand, etc.

Start by choosing a template for your post or searching for something more specific. Search by social network name to see a list of post types on each network.

Next, you can choose a template. Choose from hundreds of templates that are ready to go, with customizable photos, text, and other elements.

You can start your design by choosing from a variety of ready-made templates, searching for a template matching your needs, or working with a blank template.

Inside the Canva designer, the Elements tab gives you access to lines and shapes, graphics, photos, videos, audio, charts, photo frames, and photo grids.The search box on the Elements tab lets you search everything on Canva.

To begin with, Canva has a large library of elements to choose from. To find them, be specific in your search query. You may also want to search in the following tabs to see various elements separately:

The Photos tab lets you search for and choose from millions of professional stock photos for your templates.

You can replace the photos in our templates to create a new look. This can also make the template more suited to your industry.

You can find photos on other stock photography sites like pexel, pixabay and many more or simply upload your own photos.

When you choose an image, Canva’s photo editing features let you adjust the photo’s settings (brightness, contrast, saturation, etc.), crop, or animate it.

The Text tab lets you add headings, normal text, and graphical text to your design.

When you click on  text, you'll see options to adjust the font, font size, color, format, spacing, and text effects (like shadows).

Create an animated image or video by adding audio to capture user’s attention in social news feeds.

Want to create your own videos? Choose from thousands of stock video clips. You’ll find videos that range upto 2 minutes

On the Background tab, you’ll find free stock photos to serve as backgrounds on your designs. Change out the background on a template to give it a more personal touch.

The Styles tab lets you quickly change the look and feel of your template with just a click. And if you have a Canva Pro subscription, you can upload your brand’s custom colors and fonts to ensure designs stay on brand.

#9782. Debugging Missing Results in a Multistage Search Pipeline

Senior software engineer building search, ranking, personalization, and ML infrastructure. I write about AI evaluation and distributed systems

Senior software engineer building search, ranking, personalization, and ML infrastructure. I write about AI evaluation and distributed systems

Senior software engineer building search, ranking, personalization, and ML infrastructure. I write about AI evaluation and distributed systems

A reader searches a library catalog for a book the library definitely owns. The request succeeds, latency looks normal, and the results page is full of plausible alternatives. The expected book is missing.

The ranking model is the obvious suspect. But tweaking scores cannot help if the book never reaches the model. It might be absent from the serving index. Retrieval might cut it off at a candidate limit. A filter might reject it on a technicality. Or the page might lose it during assembly. Each explanation needs different evidence and a different fix.

The argument of this piece: before you tune anything, find the first stage where your candidate stopped progressing. Everything else follows from that.

A good score in a report can be misleading here. A book that would have ranked first still cannot appear if it was never in the ranking input. Counterfactual scores do not describe the actual request.

Most search systems pass candidates through the same five stages. A missing result means the candidate left this chain at some point, or never entered it.

Walk these in flow order. Later stages inherit everything earlier stages did wrong. The first link that broke is the one to fix.

“Search quality got worse” is too broad to debug. You need one specific request and one specific item: item b04 was missing from request R, which used index snapshot S and configuration C. That gives you something to reproduce.

Preserve the context: normalized query, locale, eligibility rules, experiment assignment, and personalization inputs. A replay against today's index with default settings may describe a different request. Keep sensitive inputs under access control.

Request timings tell you where a system spent time, not where the result set changed. For diagnosis, you want each stage's decision on a candidate: kept, dropped, or never seen, plus the reason.

A compact event record works well: request ID, candidate ID, stage, action, and a reason code. Ranking events can add score and position; display events can note items cut by the page limit. Keep shared context such as index, model, and code versions in a request-level record so you do not repeat it per event.

Two cautions. First, a reason code records what the code decided, not that the decision was right. An event saying language mismatch only helps if you check the stored value, the requested value, and the intended comparison rule. Otherwise it just labels a wrong decision.

Second, some candidates have no events at all. If retrieval never emitted the item, there is nothing to record downstream, and the absence of events cannot distinguish an indexing failure from a cutoff or a query mismatch. Keep two extra facts for those cases: does the item exist in the request's snapshot, and where does it sit in the full retrieval ordering? A position beyond the candidate limit explains the silence. In production, use a targeted lookup against the same snapshot or a controlled replay, and write down what the diagnostic actually proved. Say unknown where the evidence runs out.

Consider a fictional library catalog where our target book is fourth in retrieval order but would rank first on relevance if it reached the ranker. Three separate faults remove it, each at a different stage.

The first fault is a stale index snapshot: the current catalog has the book, but the snapshot the request served from omits it. A membership check against that snapshot comes back false, stopping the investigation before retrieval or ranking. That establishes absence from that snapshot, nothing more. Ingestion failures, rejected documents, or a request routed to an older generation could each be upstream causes, so you need ingestion and routing evidence to tell them apart. Verify fixes against the snapshot the request actually used.

The second fault is a filter rejecting an eligible item. The book reaches retrieval with stored language en, but a bad configuration requests EN and compares with case-sensitive equality, so the filter event reports a language mismatch. Comparing the stored value against the intended lowercase contract exposes the mistake. The telltale symptom is breadth: this fault rejects every retrieved book, so the displayed set is empty. The fix follows the field's contract. Do not normalize blindly, though; some identifiers are case-sensitive by design, and authorization rules deserve stronger guarantees than a convenient string conversion.

The third fault is retrieval truncating the candidate set. The book is in the snapshot and fourth in retrieval order, but the configuration retrieves only three candidates. The filter never receives it, so there is no filter event at all. Membership lookup, retrieval position, and the configured limit together locate the loss. In production, raising candidate counts adds retrieval, feature-loading, and ranking cost, so measure cost and coverage before making it the general answer.

When candidate IDs are stable, a baseline run and the changed run are easy to compare. Walk both histories in pipeline order and stop at the first divergence. If the snapshots differ, a later score difference is probably a consequence of changed inputs, not a model problem. If retrieval is identical but filtering differs, compare filter inputs and rules before you retrain anything.

Also mark your evidence complete or truncated. A request that timed out halfway should not look like a complete history.

Recording every candidate transition for every request grows with traffic and candidate counts. Sample bounded diagnostics, cap the event budget, and keep retention short. Keep lightweight stage counts everywhere, and collect detailed histories only for selected investigations.

When one of those lacks evidence, report the gap. The next useful change may be better instrumentation, not a different ranking model.

Most missing-result investigations end where they should have started: the stage that quietly dropped the candidate. Ask where it stopped progressing, collect evidence at that boundary, and the fix usually becomes obvious.

#9781. Carrier firmware vs unlocked firmware: what actually changes when you flash the other one

Two Galaxy phones with the same model name can run firmware that behaves differently. One shows a carrier logo when it starts up, comes with carrier apps, and waits longer for updates. The other boots clean, has no carrier apps, and often gets updates first. The difference is not the phone. It is the firmware, and it is possible to switch from one to the other by flashing. Before doing that, it helps to know exactly what changes, because the switch is not cosmetic.

Carrier firmware is the version of Samsung software that a mobile carrier has tested and approved for its own network. It starts as the same Samsung software as every other build, then the carrier adds its own layer: a boot logo, preinstalled carrier apps, network settings tuned for that carrier, and sometimes features the carrier wants turned on or off.

The carrier also controls the update schedule. Samsung sends the update to the carrier first, the carrier tests it on its network, and only then does it go out to phones. That testing step is the reason carrier phones often get an update weeks after unlocked phones. It is not that the phone was forgotten. It is standing in a carrier queue.

Carrier firmware also carries a specific CSC, the region code for that carrier. The CSC decides which carrier features are active, such as Wi-Fi calling, video calling, and visual voicemail. Those features work because the firmware was built for that carrier, not because the phone is special.

Unlocked firmware is the version Samsung ships for phones that are not tied to a carrier. It has no carrier logo, no carrier apps, and no carrier testing step in its update path. Samsung pushes updates to unlocked phones directly, so they usually arrive first.

Unlocked firmware still has a CSC, but it is a generic one for the region rather than one for a carrier. That means it uses Samsung's default settings for features like Wi-Fi calling, which may or may not work depending on the carrier the phone is used on. Some carriers only enable Wi-Fi calling on their own firmware, so an unlocked phone on that carrier can lose the feature even though the phone supports it.

The trade is simple. Unlocked firmware is cleaner and faster to update, but it gives up the carrier specific features and settings that carrier firmware provides. For many people that trade is worth it. For others, the missing features matter more than the earlier updates.

Flashing unlocked firmware onto a carrier phone is the most common switch, and it usually works well. The phone boots without the carrier logo, the carrier apps are gone, and updates start coming straight from Samsung. The phone also stops waiting for carrier approval, so monthly patches tend to arrive sooner.

What surprises people is what else changes. Carrier features can stop working. Wi-Fi calling and video calling are the usual ones, because the carrier may only enable them on phones running its own firmware. Visual voicemail can also break, or fall back to basic voicemail. The phone still makes calls and uses mobile data normally, but the extras tied to the carrier can go quiet.

There is also a SIM lock question. If the phone is still SIM locked to its carrier, flashing unlocked firmware does not unlock it. The lock is separate from the firmware, and it stays in place. Flashing only changes the software. The phone still needs the carrier's unlock code, or to meet the carrier's unlocking conditions, before it will accept another carrier's SIM.

The flash itself needs the right firmware file. The model number must match exactly, and the CSC in the file must be the unlocked CSC for that region. Flashing a file for the wrong model is how phones get bricked, so the model number check comes first, every time.

The reverse switch is less common, but people do it when they want a carrier feature back, or when they bought a phone that was originally a carrier phone and want it to behave like one again. Flashing carrier firmware onto an unlocked phone restores the carrier logo, the carrier apps, and the carrier settings, including features like Wi-Fi calling that only work on carrier firmware.

The cost is the same trade in reverse. The phone goes back into the carrier update queue, so updates arrive later. The carrier apps return, and some of them cannot be removed, only disabled. The phone also picks up the carrier CSC, which changes the region settings to match that carrier.

One risk is specific to this direction. Some carrier firmware builds are made for phones with a different hardware variant, such as a different modem, even when the model name matches. A carrier build meant for one variant can cause network problems on another, such as weak signal or missing bands. Checking the full model number, including the letters at the end, matters more here than in most flashes.

The right choice depends on what you value. If you want updates as early as possible and a clean phone with no carrier apps, unlocked firmware is the better fit. If you rely on Wi-Fi calling, visual voicemail, or another carrier feature, carrier firmware is the safer choice, because those features are not guaranteed on unlocked firmware.

Before flashing in either direction, check three things. First, the full model number in Settings, under About phone, and confirm the firmware file matches it exactly. Second, whether the phone is SIM locked, because flashing does not remove a lock. Third, whether any feature you use daily depends on carrier firmware, since losing it after a flash is an annoying surprise.

Back up the phone before you start. Switching firmware with a regular CSC file wipes the phone, so photos, messages, and app data need to be saved first. A HOME_CSC file keeps the data but keeps the old CSC, which defeats the purpose of switching, so a wipe is part of the deal.

Carrier and unlocked firmware are the same Samsung software with different layers on top. Knowing which layer you are giving up, and which one you are gaining, is what makes the switch work instead of becoming a problem to undo.

For official firmware downloads and step-by-step flashing guides, visit SamFware, where SamFware keeps the latest stock ROMs for every Galaxy model.

#9780. Is a gas oven bad for bread?: Why a gas oven may be interfering with your go-to steaming method.

Adapted from King Arthur Baking Company’s Big Book of Bread

One of the most crucial steps for making crusty artisan-style bread comes at the very end: steaming.

Baking bread with steam is critical for achieving expansive, open-crumbed loaves with a golden, crisp crust. If you bake bread in a dry oven, the crust quickly sets, which prevents the dough from expanding to its full potential; this, in turn, leads to loaves with a denser crumb. If you introduce steam at the start of the bake, the crust remains moist and pliable and the loaf can stretch and expand before the crust sets, resulting in a lighter, more open crumb.

What’s more, steam also helps gelatinize starches on the loaf’s exterior, which helps it brown and creates an especially crispy, flavorful, and shiny loaf. (Learn more: A guide to baking bread with steam at home.)

There are many different ways to steam your bread, all of which are designed to introduce moisture to the oven during the first part of baking. The most common method involves setting a large cast-iron skillet below your baking stone or steel when you preheat the oven. After you load your bread into the oven, you immediately pour a cup or so of warm water into the preheated cast-iron skillet and quickly close the door so the steam doesn’t escape.

This method works great, with one exception: It’s not effective in a gas oven.

If you have a gas oven, it’s very hard to add sufficient steam. By design, gas ovens vent out effluence, meaning whatever steam you add is very quickly vented out of the oven chamber. This is particularly true if you steam your bread by pouring hot water into a cast-iron skillet, as outlined above. All the water quickly dissipates, and there’s not enough moisture left to enhance the crust.

But all is not lost. There is a workaround.

If you’re steaming bread in a gas oven, you need to use a preheated covered baker, such as a Dutch oven. Instead of adding an additional water source, the lidded vessel traps the steam that escapes from the loaf as it bakes, becoming a kind of self-steaming oven. Because the steam is sealed in, the gas oven won’t vent it out.

You can use a Dutch oven for a round, boule-shaped loaf, or any other form of covered baker, like the Brod & Taylor Bread Steel for elongated, bâtard-shaped loaves. (There’s also a round version of the Bread Steel available.)

For more guidance on this method, see our previous blogs, Bread baking in a Dutch oven and For crispy, crackle crusts, put a lid on it.

When you load your dough into the oven, slip a few ice cubes between the parchment beneath your loaf and the pan to give the loaf an extra initial burst of steam. Just don’t skip the parchment beneath the dough. Otherwise, the extra water from the melting ice may cause your bread to stick to the pot.

#9779. Vibe-Coded App Security Holes to Close Before Real Users

Posted on Nov 8 • Originally published at israr-kundi.web.app

Vibe-coded app security holes are the gaps your AI builder left open while making the app work. Before real users sign up, close four of them: open database tables, secrets in front-end code, auth checks that point the wrong way, and production settings never switched on.

Your app works. You typed what you wanted, the AI tool built it, and it looks right. People can sign up, add details, and pay. So the question is simple: can anyone else read all of it?

In June 2026, Symbiotic Security scanned 1,072 vibe-coded apps using Supabase. 98% had at least one flaw, 16% a critical one, and only 26 were clean. On 172, anyone could delete records without signing in; on 39, anyone could read every table. UpGuard reported the same pattern on 25 September 2026: 16,326 Supabase databases had tables readable from the public internet with no sign-in, out of roughly 300,000 domains scanned, and over half showed signs of personal data inside.

An AI builder aims for a working demo, not a locked door. It writes the feature, watches it run, and moves on. Security checks are not part of that loop unless you ask for them.

Tables are the clearest example. One made in the Supabase dashboard gets Row Level Security switched on by default; one made with raw SQL does not, and raw SQL is how AI tools make tables. UpGuard traced the open databases back to exactly that gap.

Keys follow the same pattern. The tool needs a key to talk to the database, so it pastes the key into the code where it can reach it — code that ships to the browser, where anyone can copy it out. In the Symbiotic scan, 308 apps had their Supabase key in their JavaScript, and 24 had another API key in their source code.

Auth guards get written the wrong way round too. In February 2026, The Register reported on one Lovable-built education app with 16 vulnerabilities, six critical, that exposed 18,697 user records including 14,928 unique email addresses. Missing RLS and inverted auth guards were the cause: the checks existed, but they let the wrong people through.

Work through these in order. Each step takes minutes, and each closes a hole the scans above keep finding.

List every table with Row Level Security switched off. In the Supabase dashboard, check each table in the public schema, or run this query: select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname = 'public' and rowsecurity = false; Every table that shows up is readable by anyone with your public key if your project uses the old automatic grants (all projects created before 30 May 2026 do). Switch RLS on for each one, then write policies that only let a signed-in user touch their own rows — one each for read, add, change, delete. Do not write a policy that says using (true): it switches RLS on and lets everyone through — the same as having no RLS at all. It is also the fix an AI assistant writes most often when a query fails, so check for it even if RLS looks on.

Search your code for every key, then sort them into two piles. The publishable key, sometimes called the anon key, is designed to be public, so it can stay in front-end code. Your data is protected by RLS policies, not by hiding that key. The service_role key, and any key labelled secret or private, must never sit in front-end code: it bypasses RLS. Move anything needing one behind your own server or a server function, and rotate every key that was ever in client code — the old key is already out there, in every copy that shipped. Do not just move a secret key into a different file in the same front-end folder: the browser still downloads that file, so the key is still public.

Test every action while signed out. Open a private browser window and try to read, change, and delete a record without signing in. If any of it works, the guard is missing or backwards. Check the admin pages and API endpoints too, not just the screens users see. In a March 2026 VibeWrench scan of 100 vibe-coded apps, 21% had no authentication on their endpoints. Check storage too: a public bucket serves every file to anyone with the link.

Switch on the production protections, then re-check after every change. Turn on CSRF protection: 70% of the VibeWrench apps were missing it. Run the Supabase Security Advisor and fix every RLS warning it lists. Then repeat this check after each round of AI changes: each fix can quietly reopen a hole. The holes come back when nobody is watching.

Get help if a service_role key was ever live in shipped code, or if your checks show records already readable. Get help too if you cannot tell which tables are open, or if your policies still let a signed-out test read them. Guessing at access rules is how the holes stay open.

If this is your app, contact me through https://israr-kundi.web.app

#9775. How to sign a PDF with a photo of your signature, without printing it

The usual way to sign a PDF that someone sent you is to print it, sign the paper, and scan it back, which takes a printer and a scanner for a single line of ink. The other common route, drawing your name with a trackpad, gives a signature that doesn't look like yours. A third option is a photo: sign a sheet of white paper once, take a picture, and let the PDF editor keep only the ink. The steps below do that in the PDF Editor of the osFoundry desktop app, on an example freelance agreement.

Sign a plain white sheet with the pen you normally use and take a photo of it in bright, even light. The editor's own hint says the same: use the flash if the room is dim. The photo only has to be readable; it doesn't have to be straight or cropped, because the next step finds the signature itself.

Open the PDF, then choose All tools, Fill & Sign and Add signature. The Create signature dialog has four tabs; pick Scan, click Choose photo and select the picture.

The editor draws a frame around the signature and shows the result underneath: just the ink, on a see-through background, with the paper gone. It keeps what is darker than the paper, which is why even light matters. If the preview looks thin or has paper specks in it, the Ink sensitivity slider (it starts at 50) adjusts how dark something has to be to count as ink. Click Apply, and the signature is saved under Sign yourself in the Fill & Sign panel, ready for every later document.

Click the signature line in the document. The signature lands there at a sensible size, and a drag moves it if it sits a little high or low.

At this point the signature is a sticker on top of the page. It is stored as a stamp annotation, the same kind of object as a comment or a highlight, so another PDF reader can select it, drag it somewhere else or delete it. That is fine while you are still deciding where it goes, and not what you want in the file you send.

Open the command search at the top (Find tools and commands, or Cmd+K), type Flatten and choose Flatten comments.

Flattening turns annotations into part of the page. The signature is no longer an object sitting above the document but drawn in the page content, like the printed text. Save the file with the save button in the toolbar, and it is ready to send back.

On the example file, reading the saved PDF back with PyMuPDF showed 0 annotations and one image on the page, a 1032 × 198 px ink picture with its own transparency, where the version before flattening held one stamp annotation on top of the page.

A signature drawn this way is a picture of a signature, which is what most freelance and business PDFs ask for. It is not a cryptographic digital signature, and a contract that requires one needs a different tool.

#9772. Logout Does Not Necessarily Clear the Browser's Back-Forward Snapshot

The risk grows with shared devices and sensitive dashboards. A user opens an invoice or account page, signs out, and hands the device to another person. The second person presses Back. If the page is restored from bfcache, the old DOM may appear before the application has checked the session again. Client-side code that only runs during initial load may not refresh the view. Even when the application redirects quickly, the restored snapshot can reveal information during the transition.

Cache-Control: no-store is one relevant control. MDN notes that a response with no-store is excluded from bfcache in supported browsers. The header also has broader effects on HTTP caching and performance, so teams should apply it to pages whose content is genuinely sensitive rather than every response. no-cache is not equivalent because it permits storage and requires revalidation before reuse. The browser's bfcache and the HTTP cache are related but distinct mechanisms.

Client-side lifecycle handling adds another layer. The pageshow event includes a persisted property that can identify a restored page. A logout flow can mark the local state as signed out, replace sensitive DOM content, and make a fresh authorization request before showing protected data. However, a JavaScript handler is not a substitute for the server rejecting the old session. The application should also abort or reconnect WebSocket and event streams after restoration.

The deployment needs a test that matches the threat. Sign in with account A, open a sensitive page, sign out, navigate Back, and inspect what is visible. Repeat with the network offline after logout and after a short delay. Check whether the page appears from bfcache, whether the session is rejected, and whether cached API responses remain accessible. Test both the browser's rendered view and the underlying requests.

Developers should also audit client storage. IndexedDB, localStorage, in-memory stores, and service worker caches can retain data even when a page is no longer in bfcache. A logout flow that clears one storage mechanism but leaves another can produce the same disclosure. Define a data retention policy for each storage surface and remove sensitive values that are no longer needed. Avoid placing authorization decisions in client storage that the server cannot verify.

The safest design assumes that logout is a distributed state change. The server revokes the session, the client clears its sensitive surfaces, and the browser is instructed not to keep a restorable snapshot of the protected page. Each layer has limits, and none should be treated as complete alone. The practical goal is to make the old page useless even if the browser shows it briefly.

#9770. Ahrefs vs SEMrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Use?

SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.

If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.

In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.

SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.

The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension

Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The company was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.

Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.

Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.

In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.

The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.

Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include:

When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic.

Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.

When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.

If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.

Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.

The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.

Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:

You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.

It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.

SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:

The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.

Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.

Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.

Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.

SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.

Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you plan on using for future content rather than those you use now.

When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms.

The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine.

Ahrefs supports several features, including:

SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear.

Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike.

If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations.

Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you.

Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more.

Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have.

To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours.

SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including:

Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites.

SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more.

The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets.

SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.

When it comes to keyword data research, you will become confused about which one to choose.

Both tools are great. Choose the one which meets your requirements and if you have any experience using either Ahrefs or SEMrush let me know in the comment section which works well for you.

#9765. Microsoft's AI Frontiers Research Group Is Gone — and Its Founder Left With It

Posted on Nov 8 • Originally published at rohantechofficial.com

Microsoft's flagship AI research group is finished. John Langford, the Microsoft Research leader who helped create AI Frontiers, announced on November 6 that he has left the company — and that the group itself is over.

The roughly 50-person team behind the AutoGen agent framework and the Fara computer-use agent was folded into Microsoft AI in early September. Langford says the two groups simply could not work together: one was built for research, the other for scaling.

In a post titled "The End of AI Frontiers" on his blog Machine Learning (Theory), Langford explained that the group was set up inside Microsoft Research after ChatGPT launched, to run research in a more coordinated way. Microsoft AI, led by former Inflection executives, centres on scaling — bigger models, better training data, longer training runs — and Langford says that made the two groups incompatible.

He writes that he placed his team members as best he could and left, that every other founding AI Frontiers leader reached a similar conclusion, and that there will be no AI Frontiers internships next year. Microsoft has not commented publicly.

AI Frontiers, formed in 2023, worked on agents, core models and shared infrastructure. Its best-known work is AutoGen, one of the most popular open-source multi-agent frameworks, and Fara, a computer-use agent. The team also worked on model research — the Full Bandwidth Transformer, Next Latent and Dion3 — plus an edge-scale pretraining pipeline.

That is what makes this more than an org-chart story. When a research lab closes, the code stays — but the people who understood it leave. Langford considered returning to Microsoft Research, and says he did not go back because research there has no clear path to use.

The tension Langford describes is the central argument in AI today: does progress come from bigger models and more compute, or from new ideas? Microsoft AI's leadership has bet on the first answer. Langford argues research still pays — he points to tests where a Full Bandwidth Transformer variant matched a model twice its size, which would halve training and inference costs.

For developers, this is the practical question. AutoGen was already winding down: the last release of autogen-agentchat on PyPI was version 0.7.5 in September 2025, and on October 16 a change to the AutoGen repository stated plainly that "Microsoft is not providing bug fixes, security fixes, new features, or support for this project."

The Fara repository is MIT-licensed and not archived, with its last push in September. But with the research group around them gone, anyone building on these frameworks should plan as if support is finished — because, by Microsoft's own README, it already is.

A vendor's org chart is part of your AI stack. Agent frameworks can lose their team overnight — and this week is a reminder to stay model-agnostic and check who is actually maintaining the code you depend on.

Are you searching for an ecomerce platform to help you build an online store and sell products?

In this Sellfy review, we'll talk about how this eCommerce platform can let you sell digital products while keeping full control of your marketing.

And the best part? Starting your business can be done in just five minutes.

Let us then talk about the Sellfy platform and all the benefits it can bring to your business.

Sellfy is an eCommerce solution that allows digital content creators, including writers, illustrators, designers, musicians, and filmmakers, to sell their products online. Sellfy provides a customizable storefront where users can display their digital products and embed "Buy Now" buttons on their website or blog. Sellfy product pages enable users to showcase their products from different angles with multiple images and previews from Soundcloud, Vimeo, and YouTube. Files of up to 2GB can be uploaded to Sellfy, and the company offers unlimited bandwidth and secure file storage. Users can also embed their entire store or individual project widgets in their site, with the ability to preview how widgets will appear before they are displayed.

Sellfy is a powerful e-commerce platform that helps you personalize your online storefront. You can add your logo, change colors, revise navigation, and edit the layout of your store. Sellfy also allows you to create a full shopping cart so customers can purchase multiple items. And Sellfy gives you the ability to set your language or let customers see a translated version of your store based on their location.

Sellfy gives you the option to host your store directly on its platform, add a custom domain to your store, and use it as an embedded storefront on your website. Sellfy also optimizes its store offerings for mobile devices, allowing for a seamless checkout experience.

Sellfy allows creators to host all their products and sell all of their digital products on one platform. Sellfy also does not place storage limits on your store but recommends that files be no larger than 5GB. Creators can sell both standard and subscription-based products in any file format that is supported by the online marketplace. Customers can purchase products instantly after making a purchase – there is no waiting period.

You can organize your store by creating your product categories, sorting by any characteristic you choose. Your title, description, and the image will be included on each product page. In this way, customers can immediately evaluate all of your products. You can offer different pricing options for all of your products, including "pay what you want," in which the price is entirely up to the customer. This option allows you to give customers control over the cost of individual items (without a minimum price) or to set pricing minimums—a good option if you're in a competitive market or when you have higher-end products. You can also offer set prices per product as well as free products to help build your store's popularity.

Sellfy is ideal for selling digital content, such as ebooks. But it does not allow you to copyrighted material (that you don't have rights to distribute).

Sellfy offers several ways to share your store, enabling you to promote your business on different platforms. Sellfy lets you integrate it with your existing website using "buy now" buttons, embed your entire storefront, or embed certain products so you can reach more people. Sellfy also enables you to connect with your Facebook page and YouTube channel, maximizing your visibility.

Sellfy is a simple online platform that allows customers to buy your products directly through your store. Sellfy has two payment processing options: PayPal and Stripe. You will receive instant payments with both of these processors, and your customer data is protected by Sellfy's secure (PCI-compliant) payment security measures. In addition to payment security, Sellfy provides anti-fraud tools to help protect your products including PDF stamping, unique download links, and limited download attempts.

To expand functionality and make your e-commerce store run more efficiently, Sellfy offers several integrations. Google Analytics and Webhooks, as well as integrations with Patreon and Facebook Live Chat, are just a few of the options available. Sellfy allows you to connect to Zapier, which gives you access to hundreds of third-party apps, including tools like Mailchimp, Trello, Salesforce, and more.

Sellfy has its benefits and downsides, but fortunately, the pros outweigh the cons.

#9761. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.

As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.

This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.

Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.

Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.

Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. #9752. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9746. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9745. 3 Personality Traits Associated With Infidelity

Up to 50% of people admit cheating on their partner.

Up to 50% of people admit cheating on their partner.

People who are low on conscientiousness are more likely to cheat on their partner, research finds.

People who are not conscientious are careless, badly organised and find it hard to resist temptation.

People who are more extraverted are also more likely to cheat on their partner, the researchers found.

It is probably because extraverted people have a wider social circle and so more opportunities to cheat.

Also, extraverts are impulsive, sensation-seekers who can easily succumb to their desires.

The conclusions come from a survey of 208 people, who were asked about their relationships and whether they had cheated.

Up to 50% of people admit cheating on their partner, the authors write:

“Early studies reported that by the age of 40, 50% of all married men and more than 25% of all married women have engaged in extramarital sexual behavior.

Three decades later, an estimated 50% of men continued to engage in sexual and/or emotional extramarital relations while 40% of women engaged in similar relationships.”

The results of the study revealed that cheaters tend to be low in conscientiousness, extraverted and open to experience.

Extraverts tend to seek out stimulation, the authors write:

“Extroverts may be inclined to cheat to obtain stimulation and prevent boredom.

Extroversion may also facilitate less investment in the relationship when those with this trait seek out others for stimulation, thereby decreasing commitment and resulting in cheating behaviours.”

The third personality trait associated with infidelity is openness to experience.

Openness to experience is linked to intellect and creativity.

“…cheaters may perceive themselves as having stronger intellect and stronger creativity compared to that of their partners, leading them to seek out partners that may be a better, that is, similar, match.”

The study was published in the journal Current Psychology (Orzeck & Lung, 2005).

#9744. No Beer, No Problem: Add A Splash Of This Drink For The Crunchiest Onion Rings

A top-tier onion ring brings together several textural qualities into one bite. You want enough heft to encase the slivers of allium, yet a crunchy consistency that's delicate. Each bite should contain both onion and batter, and while seasoning should be present, the onion's internal sweetness should still come through. It's a complex balance to get right, with beer often used as a cornerstone of the batter.

The beverage lends several advantages to onion rings: The hops and malt add flavor, the alcohol evaporates quickly during frying, and — most importantly — the carbonation creates an airy batter that translates to crunchiness. However, if you're not keen on adding a brew to your onion ring recipe, no fear: Sparkling water is a terrific alternative. Just like beer, the carbonation works its textural magic. And when used alongside rice flour (a tempura influence), you'll produce some of the crispiest onion rings, with an even more delicate texture.

It's critical to pour the sparkling water in as cold as possible — temperature control is essential for optimal crispness. As a result, you'll want to incorporate the water right out of the fridge, at the conclusion of batter preparation. Stir until the batter is homogeneous and on the liquidy side, similar to pancake or waffle batter in consistency. And you can also dredge the onions in flour separately first to make sure the breading sticks. Put the two elements together, deep-fry, and you'll get an onion ring rendition that is no less successful than a beer-based one.

Unlike beer and other flavored carbonated beverages, sparkling water's neutral flavor can be used to your advantage. Such a batter comes out lighter and without much added flavor, letting you tweak the seasonings to your liking. A rendition can be kept to a straightforward salt-only seasoning, which really puts the onions front and center. Or you can go with more flavorful spices like onion and garlic powder, paprika, and a dash of cayenne for heat. Don't rule out using some dried herbs in the batter, either; parsley flakes lend a nice herbal touch, for example. Apply seasoning both to the batter and after cooking to ensure comprehensive flavoring.

Want to up the crisp even further? Reach for some starchy ingredients other than flour and cornstarch. Dry potato flakes will lend your onion rings a pleasant starchy spin, and for an extra-golden-brown character, coat the dish with panko. Without beer in the mix, you can still achieve a light, airy texture. Serve them alongside homemade ranch, and it's an onion ring composition you'll want to make again and again.

#9741. Add Cowboy Candy To Your Next Grilled Cheese For Triple The Flavor

Making the best grilled cheese can be serious business. And though the modern grilled cheese didn't take off until the 1920s — when commercially sliced bread and process cheese made it an affordable household staple — one perfect add-on for your next sandwich carries a classic frontier spirit. It's called cowboy candy — sugared and pickled jalapeño peppers — and each slice adds an incredible amount of flavor to your meal.

If you like the sweet and sour mix of bread and butter pickles, and you can handle a decent hit of spiciness, you'll love cowboy candy. When jalapeños are pickled, the brine can mellow their heat, so you won't just get a blast of intense spiciness. You'll get crunchy, vegetal, and herbaceous notes; some nice tang from the vinegar; plus a hit of sweetness. And it goes with just about any cheese you want to put on your sando. Cheddar or Monterey Jack are classic American options. If you want more nuttiness, you can try Gruyère, or give Havarti a go for some nice buttery flavor that would also be delicious with caramelized onions. And adding some spicy chorizo will make it a full meal.

The history of cowboy candy begins in the Lone Star State. WHH Ranch, which is based in Texas, claims to be the originator of the condiment and the oldest family-owned cannery in the state. These days, you can order a variety of cowboy candy versions from its website.

If you want to make cowboy candy at home, it's not hard to do on your own. You're going to need a mix of sugar, vinegar, and pickling spices. The mixture will cook down into a thick syrup to give the peppers a nice sugary coating that turns a regular spicy grilled cheese into a masterful mix of flavors. For the spices, you can go the standard route with mustard seeds, celery seeds, and turmeric for the tasty bread and butter pickle style. But a little dried or fresh dill will get you closer to a classic dill pickle flavor, and some chipotle pepper powder will add more smokiness. If you want more of a pungent tang, you can add some apple cider vinegar.

When you're making your cowboy candy grilled cheese, think about what cheeses will blend best with the sweet, spicy, savory flavor. Maybe try a nice sourdough or thick Texas toast, and don't be afraid to try some other protein additions. Turn it into a taco-inspired sandwich with some seasoned ground beef, or use up the leftovers from your rotisserie chicken. Just get that cowboy candy for your next grilled cheese, and from there, you can pile on the flavor.

#9739. 2 Supplements That Significantly Reduce Heart Disease And Cancer Risk

The most recent trial confirms that two nutrients can reduce deaths from heart attacks and cancer.

The most recent trial confirms that two nutrients can reduce deaths from heart attacks and cancer.

Omega-3 fatty acids from fish oil can significantly reduce heart attacks and vitamin D supplementation can significantly lower the number of deaths caused by different types of cancer.

Researchers studied 26,000 American adults in the VITAL clinical trial for five years to see if fish oil or vitamin D would definitely ward off cardiovascular disease or cancer.

The outcomes were reassuring: marine omega-3 fatty acid intake was linked to a significant drop in heart attacks.

One-and-half servings per week of dietary fish intake showed the maximum heart health benefits, but higher dietary fish intake didn’t help more.

The greatest decrease in heart attacks was seen in African-Americans.

The benefit of 1 gram of omega-3 fish oil supplementation showed a small decrease in major cardiovascular events like stroke and death from cardiovascular disease.

Vitamin D3 or cholecalciferol intake at a dose of 2000 IU per day showed a significant decrease of death from cancer for those who took it for at least two years.

However, supplementation with vitamin D3 capsules didn’t significantly lower incidence of any type of cancer or cardiovascular disease.

Dr. JoAnn Manson, the study’s first author, said:

“The pattern of findings suggests a complex balance of benefits and risks for each intervention and points to the need for additional research to determine which individuals may be most likely to derive a net benefit from these supplements.”

Dr. Stephanie Faubion, NAMS medical director, said:

“With heart disease and cancer representing the most significant health threats to women, it is imperative that we continue to study the viability of options that prevent these diseases and help women survive them.”

The 1 gram omega-3 fish oil supplementation used in the VITAL clinical trial was Omacor, a prescription medicine for adults.

The capsule contains 840 milligrams marine omega-3 fatty acids, of which 465 mg is eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and 375 mg is docosahexaenoic acid (DHA).

The study was presented at the North American Menopause Society (NAMS) Annual Meeting in Chicago (Manson et al., 2019).

With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and company-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.
